'''Jaw-Shen Tsai''' ({{lang-zh|t=蔡兆申}}; born February 8, 1952) is a Taiwan-born American [[physicist]] specializing in low-temperature solid-state physics.<ref name="JapanTimes2002" /><ref name="AcademiaSinica" /><ref name="Hattori2023" /> He is known for pioneering research on superconducting qubits and their quantum control. In 1999, he, [[Yasunobu Nakamura]], and their colleagues achieved the first demonstration of qubit operation in a superconducting circuit.<ref name="JapanAcademy2023" />

He has conducted research at [[NEC]] and [[RIKEN]], and was appointed a professor at the [[Tokyo University of Science]] in 2015 and a chair professor at [[National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University]] in 2025.<ref name="NECProfile2023" /><ref name="AcademiaSinica" />

== Early life and education ==
Tsai was born in [[Taipei]], Taiwan, on February 8, 1952.<ref name="JapanTimes2002" /><ref name="Hattori2023">{{cite web
 |url=https://www.hattori-hokokai.or.jp/pdf/press-release93.pdf
 |title=2023年（第93回）服部報公会「報公賞」が決定
 |publisher=Hattori Hokokai Foundation
 |date=2023-09-05
 |format=PDF
 |language=ja
 |access-date=2026-09-05
}}</ref> He earned a [[Bachelor of Arts]] degree in physics from the [[University of California, Berkeley]], in 1975 and a [[PhD]] in physics from [[Stony Brook University]] in 1983.<ref name="AcademiaSinica" />

== Career ==
In 1983, Tsai became a research scientist at NEC's Microelectronics Research Laboratories. He subsequently held positions as a fellow at the company's Fundamental Research Laboratories and Nano Electronics Research Laboratories.<ref name="NECProfile2023">{{cite web
 |url=https://www.nec.com/en/press/202310/images/1001-01-01.pdf
 |title=Profile and Detailed Achievements of the Group A Recipients of the 2023 C&C Prize
 |publisher=NEC
 |year=2023
 |format=PDF
 |access-date=2026-09-05
}}</ref>

In 2001, he took on a concurrent appointment as team leader of RIKEN's Macroscopic Quantum Coherence Team.<ref name="AcademiaSinica" /> His later positions at RIKEN included group director of the Single Quantum Dynamics Research Group and team leader of the Superconducting Quantum Simulation Research Team.<ref name="NECProfile2023" />

He was appointed a professor at the [[Tokyo University of Science]] in 2015 and a chair professor at [[National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University]] in 2025.<ref name="AcademiaSinica" />

== Research ==
In 1999, Tsai, [[Yasunobu Nakamura]], and Yu. A. Pashkin observed quantum oscillations in a small superconducting circuit known as a [[Cooper-pair box]], demonstrating electrical control of a qubit in a solid-state electronic device. The results were published in ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]''.<ref name="Nakamura1999">{{cite journal
 |author1=Y. Nakamura
 |author2=Yu. A. Pashkin
 |author3=J. S. Tsai
 |title=Coherent control of macroscopic quantum states in a single-Cooper-pair box
 |journal=Nature
 |volume=398
 |pages=786–788
 |date=1999-04-29
 |doi=10.1038/19718
 |arxiv=cond-mat/9904003
}}</ref>

In 2003, Tsai and collaborators observed quantum oscillations in two coupled superconducting charge qubits.<ref name="Pashkin2003">{{cite journal
 |author1=Yu. A. Pashkin
 |author2=T. Yamamoto
 |author3=O. Astafiev
 |author4=Y. Nakamura
 |author5=D. V. Averin
 |author6=J. S. Tsai
 |title=Quantum oscillations in two coupled charge qubits
 |journal=Nature
 |volume=421
 |pages=823–826
 |date=2003-02-20
 |doi=10.1038/nature01365
 |arxiv=cond-mat/0212314
}}</ref> In a separate study published that year, Tsai and collaborators demonstrated conditional gate operation using two superconducting charge qubits.<ref name="Yamamoto2003">{{cite journal
 |author1=T. Yamamoto
 |author2=Yu. A. Pashkin
 |author3=O. Astafiev
 |author4=Y. Nakamura
 |author5=J. S. Tsai
 |title=Demonstration of conditional gate operation using superconducting charge qubits
 |journal=Nature
 |volume=425
 |pages=941–944
 |date=2003-10-30
 |doi=10.1038/nature02015
 |arxiv=cond-mat/0311067
}}</ref>

His research has also included the generation and detection of single microwave photons using superconducting quantum circuits.<ref name="NECProfile2023" /> The Japan Academy has recognized Nakamura and Tsai's work as a pioneering contribution to the development of superconducting quantum computing.<ref name="JapanAcademy2023" />
